## Physical dynamics guide the operating decision

An operating or manufacturing decision changes the subsequent trajectory of a physical system. I study models that predict that trajectory and how prediction errors affect the decision. Water-energy systems and precision materials manufacturing provide two settings for this work. The projects below connect these physical processes to [learning dynamics and Model2Action](/research/).

## A. Physical dynamics

{{< include ../_includes/dynamics-applications.qmd >}}

### Water-energy dynamics in data centers {#water-energy-dynamics}

My engineering interests lie in water-energy systems, with a current emphasis on the dynamics and sustainable operation of integrated multi-energy systems serving data centers. I am interested in how changes in computing demand affect cooling and energy supply over time. Dynamic optimization relates these responses to operating decisions that account for energy and water use alongside carbon emissions.

### Process dynamics in precision materials manufacturing {#precision-materials-manufacturing}

Processing conditions influence how material structure evolves over time. I work with [Professor Fengqi You](https://www.peese.org/professor/) to model this evolution and optimize the sequence of processing conditions for a target structure.

The current material system couples initiated chemical vapor deposition (iCVD) with liquid crystals (LC). I formulate dynamic models of the process and investigate neural operators that approximate its evolving state. The predicted trajectories and their sensitivities to process inputs support the optimization of processing conditions.

## B. Learning dynamics

A dynamic model used in control must predict how the state responds to candidate inputs over the relevant horizon. I investigate neural operators for these predictions and evaluate how their errors grow during a rollout. Sensitivities to process inputs connect the learned trajectories to optimization, while governing equations constrain the physical responses the model represents.

### Temporal response and uncertain pressure states <span class="branch">Engineering</span>

:::: {.project-study .theme-dynamics}
::: {.project-study-visual .project-study-visual-pair}
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2024.124508"><img src="/assets/images/publications/kbbcm.svg" width="800" height="500" loading="lazy" alt="KbBcM visual abstract showing lag-penalty attention and posterior residual correction"></a>
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TCSS.2023.3272330"><img src="/assets/images/publications/criticoder.svg" width="800" height="500" loading="lazy" alt="CritiCoder visual abstract separating measured pressure effects from unobserved disturbances"></a>
:::
::: {.project-study-copy}
Daily demand and network pressure expose different errors in a learned physical model. [KbBcM](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2024.124508) corrects delayed forecasts near demand turning points with lag-penalty attention and posterior residual correction. [CritiCoder](https://doi.org/10.1109/TCSS.2023.3272330) models pressure under measured inputs and residual variation associated with unmeasured disturbances. These studies examine temporal response and incomplete observation in water systems.

[Read the research summary](service-operations-planning.qmd)
:::
::::

### Multi-step energy dynamics in industrial rolling <span class="branch">Engineering</span>

:::: {.project-study .theme-process}
::: {.project-study-visual}
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TASE.2023.3299185"><img src="/assets/images/publications/series-concat.svg" width="800" height="500" loading="lazy" alt="Series-concatenation visual abstract for energy prediction across multi-step rolling"></a>
:::
::: {.project-study-copy}
Hot-strip roughing consists of an ordered sequence of rolling passes. A [DCLS-Net study](https://doi.org/10.1109/TASE.2023.3299185) predicts the energy of each pass and links those predictions through series concatenation. This study examines how the sequence of processing operations relates to its energy consumption.
:::
::::

## C. Model2Action

Model2Action connects the predicted dynamics to the inputs selected by a controller or optimizer. I study how trajectory errors affect operating cost and constraint satisfaction, and how these consequences can guide model training. The same question applies to the operation of water-energy systems and to the choice of processing conditions in materials manufacturing.

### Coupled water-energy operation under forecast uncertainty <span class="branch">Engineering</span>

:::: {.project-study .theme-decision}
::: {.project-study-visual}
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TSG.2025.3601238"><img src="/assets/images/publications/spto.svg" width="800" height="500" loading="lazy" alt="SPTO visual abstract linking a probabilistic electricity-cost forecast to a stochastic water-supply schedule"></a>
:::
::: {.project-study-copy}
Water-supply operation links when water is processed and delivered to when electricity is consumed. [SPTO](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSG.2025.3601238) trains a probabilistic electricity-cost forecast through the stochastic water-supply schedule it induces. Its SPTO+ variant uses a differentiable upper bound on the optimality gap as the loss. Operating cost and regret measure the consequences of forecast error over the scheduling horizon.

[Read the research summary](industrial-workflow-analysis.qmd)
:::
::::

### Feedback laws for constrained nonlinear dynamics <span class="branch">Engineering</span>

:::: {.project-study .theme-control}
::: {.project-study-visual .project-study-visual-pair}
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TSMC.2023.3344883"><img src="/assets/images/publications/rl-controller.svg" width="800" height="500" loading="lazy" alt="Constrained reinforcement-learning controller visual abstract"></a>
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/CDC49753.2023.10383316"><img src="/assets/images/publications/eligibility-traces.svg" width="800" height="500" loading="lazy" alt="Multiple time-scale eligibility traces visual abstract"></a>
:::
::: {.project-study-copy}
Nonlinear model predictive control initializes a controller network for discrete-time constrained systems, and a control barrier function with a nonquadratic loss enforces the state and input constraints during learning. A study of adaptive optimal control uses eligibility traces at several time scales to give the critic credit signals accumulated over different horizons.

[Constrained controller](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSMC.2023.3344883) · [Multiple time-scale eligibility traces](https://doi.org/10.1109/CDC49753.2023.10383316)
:::
::::

### Geometry-conditioned motion in physical environments <span class="branch">Robotics</span>

:::: {.project-study .theme-geometry}
::: {.project-study-visual}
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2026.133261"><img src="/assets/images/publications/drift.svg" width="800" height="500" loading="lazy" alt="DRIFT visual abstract showing LiDAR graph memory and target-directed recurrent diffusion"></a>
:::
::: {.project-study-copy}
[DRIFT](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2026.133261) stores local LiDAR geometry as graph memory and retrieves waypoint-specific context during recurrent diffusion. The study evaluates generated trajectories through endpoint error, clearance, smoothness, and runtime. This collaborative work examines how a learned action satisfies the geometric constraints of its physical environment.
:::
::::
